To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We present an asynchronous redundant SAR interleaved ADC that achieves 8b conversion at 90GS/s and 6.1ENOB at 100GS/s.
we have developed an ADC that achieves a sampling rate of up to 100GS/s with an SNDR of up to 36dB at 6.1 GHz and 33dB at 19.9 GHz input frequency while consuming only 667mW from a single supply.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of high-speed ADCs for optical communications.
the design and analysis of high-speed ADCs for the next-generation optical communication standards.
the design of high-speed CMOS ADCs and the design and analysis of high-speed CMos circuits in general.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
interleaved SARs are the best solution to achieve high-speed, moderate-resolution ADCs.
the presented ADC architecture is a promising solution for the future generation of high-speed ADCs.
interleaved SAR architectures can be used for ADCs with more then 6b resolution and sampling rates up to 90GS/s.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented ADC is the fastest ADC ever presented and the first 8b interleaved ADC in CMOS technology.
the ADC is the first CMOS ADC to achieve more than 6ENOB at more than 90GS/s and that it is the first 8b ADC to achieve more then 5ENOB at more then 90GS/s.
we have demonstrated the first CMOS ADC with a conversion rate exceeding 90GS/s in a 32nm CMOS technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed ADC architecture allows to achieve high sampling rates with a moderate resolution of 8b at a moderate power budget.
a high-speed interleaved SAR ADC architecture is feasible with moderate power consumption.
a single SAR ADC core with an asynchronous redundant architecture can be used as a building block for high-speed interleaved ADCs.
